acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's marriage with respondent No.2 was solemnized as per Hindu rites and customs. Respondent No.3 is the mother of respondent No.2. A son was born from the wedlock on 06.02.2010. However, there were disputes amongst the husband and wife. FIR No.764/2015 was filed against the petitioner at PS Ranjit Nagar, Delhi under Sections 498A/406/307 IPC by the respondent no.2.

legal_principles.principle: Compromise between parties can lead to quashing of FIR.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted by both the counsels that the petitioner and respondent Nos. 2 and 3 have settled the matter amicably and entered into compromise and dispute between the parties have since been vanished and the parties have buried their hatchet.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle disputes and withdraw criminal proceedings.
legal_principles.held: On 21.10.2016 a CRL.M.C.No.208/2016 was filed for quashing of FIR on the basis of compromise but it was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 21.10.2016.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

outcome.final_order: FIR No.764/2015 stands quashed. The parties are near relation to each other and since a decree of divorce is also granted, the petition stands disposed of.

keywords: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
use_for_drafting: quashing FIRs in domestic violence cases
